description: Neural Knights is a team of developers and problem-solvers participating in NASA Space Apps Challenge 2026. We bring skills in MERN/full-stack development, backend, AI/ML, databases, and system design. We' re building a Junior Astronaut Mission Trainer to make space science interactive and engaging. We're looking for teammates skilled in game development, Three.js/WebGL, UI/UX, 3D/animation, or space science interactive.
summary: LunaRangers is an interactive, science-driven lunar mission simulation where players take on the role of mission operators responsible for keeping a lunar mission running safely. Players investigate equipment failures, collect evidence, diagnose problems, make engineering decisions, manage critical resources such as oxygen, water, food and power, and respond to environmental hazards. Each decision produces consequences that influence the mission's progress and crew safety. The project addresses the challenge of making space science and lunar mission operations engaging and accessible through scenario-based gameplay rather than passive learning. It combines resource management, equipment troubleshooting, mission objectives, and workflows such as EVA and lunar sample collection. By connecting scientific concepts with practical decision-making, LunaRangers helps players understand the complexity of operating in an extreme lunar environment while developing problem-solving, critical-thinking, and engineering awareness.
details:
Project Details — LunaRangers

LunaRangers is an interactive lunar mission simulation that places players in the role of mission operators managing a fictional lunar mission. Players encounter mission scenarios involving equipment malfunctions, resource shortages, environmental hazards, and crew safety. They must inspect equipment, collect evidence, diagnose problems, choose appropriate actions, and observe how their decisions affect the mission.

The simulation manages interconnected resources, including oxygen, carbon dioxide, water, food, and electrical power. It also incorporates equipment repair, crew management, extravehicular activities (EVA), and lunar sample collection. Rather than presenting players with predefined answers, the project encourages investigation, experimentation, and decision-making.

Benefits and intended impact: LunaRangers makes complex space-science and engineering concepts more accessible through practical, scenario-driven experiences. It encourages critical thinking, problem-solving, resource management, and an understanding of how different spacecraft and habitat systems depend on one another. Our goal is to make learning about lunar exploration more engaging and memorable.

Technology and development: The simulation engine is being developed using TypeScript and a modular architecture. We use Node.js, npm, and Vitest for development and automated testing, with Git and GitHub for version control and team collaboration. The project also incorporates interactive game environments and visual design assets to create an immersive lunar experience.

Creativity and design considerations: The creative aspect lies in turning engineering challenges into interactive experiences where decisions have consequences. Our team considered scientific plausibility, resource dependencies, crew safety, gameplay engagement, and the balance between educational value and accessibility. We are designing the system with a flexible campaign architecture so that different mission scenarios and objectives can be introduced without rebuilding the simulation engine.
